verdict.rationale: Aider documents only one-off, user-initiated runs. `--message` does a single instruction and exits, and the unsupported Python scripting API executes one instruction. `--watch-files` reacts to AI comments a human writes, which is an alternate input method, not an autonomous trigger. Nothing documents built-in scheduling, event triggers, or always-on autonomous maintenance agents; any recurring schedule would need user-side tooling such as cron, and the autonomy 'navigator-mode' is a community third-party add-on.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously
